title: 2026 Nobel Prize in Medicine goes to optogenetics pioneers, and the committee warns against AI-brain comparisons

Questions this post answers

Who won the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine and for what discovery?

Karl Deisseroth, Peter Hegemann and Georg Nagel won for optogenetics, a technique that uses light to switch nerve cells on and off. The method traces back to channelrhodopsin, a light-sensitive protein from green algae, which Deisseroth used to make rat and mouse neurons fire in response to blue light, enabling precise control of individual cells. Developers curious about the science behind brain-computer interfaces can follow research breakthroughs like this on daily.dev.

Did the Nobel committee say AI neural networks work like the human brain?

No, the Nobel committee explicitly cautioned against that comparison, stating that the similarities between neural networks used in AI and the human brain shouldn't be exaggerated. This came in response to a reporter's question about whether optogenetics research could help explain what happens inside AI neural networks during the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine announcement.
